skills.title: My Roles and Responsibilities
skills.description: You are a student, a friend, and a family member. Pick the jobs and ways you care for others that go with each role.

skills.title: Important People, Places, Things
skills.description: Some people, places, and things matter a lot in your life. Match each one, like a teacher, a library, or a pet, to what it is for.

skills.title: My Life Events in Order
skills.description: Put big things from a life in the order they happen, like daycare, Kindergarten, then Grade 1.

skills.title: Kind and Inclusive Actions
skills.description: Pick actions that are kind and include everyone, like sharing, taking turns, and caring for Elders.

skills.title: Respect for People and Earth
skills.description: Sort ways to treat people, plants, and water with respect from ways that are not respectful.

skills.title: Roles Change by Place and Time
skills.description: Your jobs and how you act can change at home or school, and as you grow. Pick how a role changes in a new place or time.

skills.title: Events That Change My Roles
skills.description: Starting school, a new baby, or moving can change your jobs and relationships. Match each event to the change it brings.

skills.title: Comparing Life Events
skills.description: Friends and family have big events too. Sort which events are the same and which are different for different people.

skills.title: How People Affect Each Other
skills.description: What we do can make others feel happy, sad, proud, or safe. Pick how an action changes how someone feels about themselves.

skills.title: Reviving Indigenous Cultures
skills.description: First Nations, Métis, and Inuit communities are bringing back languages and traditions. Pick ways this helps people feel proud and that they belong.

skills.title: Questions About Me and My Life
skills.description: Pick a good question you could investigate about how your jobs or feelings changed after an event.

skills.title: Finding Sources About My Life
skills.description: Photos, stories, interviews, and artefacts can tell about your life. Sort which sources help answer a question.

skills.title: Maps of My Special Places
skills.description: Read a simple map of the route from home to school or a friend's house. Pick the title, legend, and directions.

skills.title: Timelines and Venn Diagrams
skills.description: Read a timeline, Venn diagram, or calendar about a child's life and pick what it shows.

skills.title: Conclusions From Evidence About Me
skills.description: Look at clues about a child's life and pick the conclusion that the clues support.

skills.title: Sharing What I Found Out
skills.description: Pick the best way to share results, and the right words like role, relationship, and identity.

skills.title: Natural and Built Features
skills.description: Sort things in a community into natural ones, like rivers and forests, and built ones, like roads and schools.

skills.title: Areas of a Community
skills.description: Match places to areas like homes, shopping areas, busy roads, and natural areas by what you see there.

skills.title: Land and Treaty Territory
skills.description: Our school sits on traditional Indigenous land and treaty territory. Pick the territory name for your school's area.

skills.title: Near, Far, Left, Right
skills.description: Use words like near, far, left, right, in front, and behind to tell where places are.

skills.title: Parts of a Map
skills.description: Label the title, legend symbols, direction arrow, and colours on a simple map, and read the map.

skills.title: Measuring With Footsteps and Blocks
skills.description: Measure with footsteps, tiles, or blocks. Pick which is longer and why the same unit must be used.

skills.title: Making a Simple Map
skills.description: Pick the symbols, scale, and legend to make a map of a route or a park, using blocks or steps for distance.

skills.title: Community Services and Workers
skills.description: Match services like the post office, clinic, and grocery store, and workers like store clerks, to the needs they meet.

skills.title: Services and Our Responsibilities
skills.description: Some services, like garbage pickup and fire services, are run by the government or community. Match each to what people must do, like sorting recycling or shovelling snow.

skills.title: How People Use Their Community
skills.description: People use nature, buildings, and services to meet needs. Pick what could happen if a park or service was missing.

skills.title: Planning to Care for Community
skills.description: Put steps for a clean-up or a garden plan in order, and pick how your actions make a place better.

skills.title: Questions About Our Community
skills.description: Pick a good question to investigate about how people change a place, like what happens if litter is left in a park.

skills.title: Gathering Community Information
skills.description: Pick the best tool, like a tally sheet, a photo, or an interview, to collect facts about a place.

skills.title: Maps of Community Features
skills.description: Read a map with symbols and a legend that shows parks, water, and shops, including Indigenous place names.

skills.title: Pictographs and Then-and-Now Photos
skills.description: Read a pictograph or compare old and new photos to see how a place has changed.

skills.title: Short and Long Term Effects
skills.description: Use evidence to pick conclusions about what people's actions did to a place, soon and later on.

skills.title: Sharing Community Findings
skills.description: Pick the best way to share what you learned, and the right words like location, map, symbol, and legend.
